corrections.current: 1910 (Year of the tower described by the Lighthouse Directory)
corrections.proposed: 1911-12 (fiscal year): 33-foot standard wooden tower and lantern erected, replacing a worn-out building
corrections.why: The Marine report for fiscal 1911-12 records the erection of a 33-foot standard wooden tower and lantern at Wolfe Island; LF gives 1911; Rowlett's 1910 does not match either. Needs a human decision about which date the record uses.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett gives 1910 for the tower; LF gives 1911 for the 33-foot wooden tower; the Marine fiscal 1911-12 report records its erection. The Marine report is the most specific source, and the story uses it.
The Coast Guard list gives 6.4 m for the structure (entry 378); the Lighthouse Directory gives 6.5 m (21 ft) for the present tower. The story gives both and does not choose.

LF places the light on Quebec Head, the north-eastern tip of Wolfe Island, and the 1877 inspection says Quebec Point. The 1887 tribute, as LF quotes it, says 'at Port Metcalfe, foot of Wolfe Island'. The sources do not settle whether the tribute describes the same light; the story flags it.

notes_for_editor: Most of the keeper history from 1862 to 1885 and the 1877 description rest on LighthouseFriends quoting Marine and Commissioners' reports that are not in the corpus (marine_ca begins in 1900). Check those originals before publication, especially the 1856 proposal and the 1877 description, both second-hand. The 1887 British Whig tribute places the light 'at Port Metcalfe, foot of Wolfe Island'; in the 1905 Marine report 'foot of Wolfe island' names a dredged cut near Kingston at the west end of the island, while the light is on the east tip. The sources do not settle whether the tribute describes this light; the story flags it and keeps LF's identification. Robert Gillespie's sole keeping 1863-1885 and the 1862-1863 keepers Thomas Kilty and Robert Gillespie come from LF only. William Gillespie's appointment date: 17 March 1885 in the 1909 and 1910 keeper lists (position-matched; the 1910 list, report p. 267, scan 269, was checked on the page image: Wolf Island, Wm. Gillespie, Mar. 17, 1885). A 1901 list and the 1915 list (fiscal 1914-15 report, scan 88, printed 81) read 16 March (OCR), so the story says 'March 1885'. The 1908 apparatus list (report p. 90, under ONTARIO) gives 'Wolf Island' with a 270-degree 5th order French lens and acetylene; it is matched by the heading. Not used: 'Southwest Wolfe island, Bay of Fundy' (New Brunswick) and the US Lighthouse Board's 'Wolf Island' (Georgia). Newspapers: 'Wolfe Island' with 'lighthouse' 1861-1915 gave 11 Chronicling America pages; the snippets were other Wolfe Islands (Magdalen Islands; ship news) except a 1896 Kingston News item, reprinted in the Hawaiian Gazette as a Dr. Williams' Pink Pills testimonial, which calls Hugh McLaren 'lighthouse keeper on Wolfe Island'. No other source names him and LF's list does not; it is not used. Recommend a human check. 'Wolfe Island' with 'Gillespie' 1861-1939 gave no hits. Storms and wrecks: none tied to this light in the corpus or the sources read, so the story has no storms chapter. Height: the 1911-12 tower was 33 ft (10 m) per the Marine report; Rowlett now gives 6.5 m (21 ft) with the lantern removed; the sources do not date the change or explain it. CCG entry 378 gives 11.3 m (height above water), 8 NM and a structure height of 6.4 m (read from the list table); the Lighthouse Directory gives 6.5 m (21 ft). The CCG's Iso W 4s matches the Directory's two seconds on and two seconds off. Ownership: LF and Rowlett say the Canadian Coast Guard owns it; Rowlett gives a private site manager. Access: road and path private; grounds and tower closed; reach by water or the ferry (Rowlett). Not checked: Parks Canada and the Directory of Federal Heritage Designations. Record: the 'built 1910' event should follow the Marine fiscal 1911-12 date (see corrections). Further checks: the 1908 apparatus entry 'Wolf Island' sits under the ONTARIO heading (report p. 90, scan 99, printed 90), checked in the corpus; the 1911-12 entry 'Erection of a 33-foot standard wooden tower and lantern, rereplacing worn-out building' sits under Wolfe island (report p. 53, scan 60). The 1877 inspection's '36 feet' is quoted in full, because the inspection does not say whether it measures the building or the light.
